mu_name_from: MuMain loads MODEL_BOOTS + i from BootMale{i+1} (ZzzOpenData.cpp line 143), so file 03 is boot index 2, which openmu's 0.75 Armors.cs names the Pad Boots. mu.db agrees: code 5634, group 11 index 2, Player/BootMale03.bmd.
why_this_one:
The only pair of boots a Budge Dragon can leave, and the last of the four armour pieces in its pool. Drop level 4, the dragon's own; the Pad Gloves beside it are 3. Together they are the whole of what the Dark Wizard's first set a level 4 monster can give up - the Pad Helm is 5, the Pants 8 and the Armor 10.

The first worn part in the tree with a cut-out sheet other than the Plate Helm's plume: boots_04b is a 32x32 TGA with real alpha, cutting away 65% of itself, and it carries the gilt fins that stand off the boot.
profile_from: Not armour, whose default is plate_steel. See profiles/soft_armour.json.

stats.note: The item's own row, copied from OpenMU's 0.75 initialiser rather than restated, with the call it came from beside it.
stats.from: openmu/src/Persistence/Initialization/Version075/Items/Armors.cs line 123. The 0.75 table, which is the version this server is being built to.
stats.call_note: ArmorInitializerBase.CreateBoots(number, slot, width, height, name, dropLevel, defense, walkSpeed, durability, strengthRequirement, agilityRequirement, darkWizardClassLevel, darkKnightClassLevel, elfClassLevel). Slot 6, so `armor.Group = (byte)(slot + 5)` makes the group 11 - the last group a character equips, and the one Prize.TakesRefinement stops at.
stats.drop_level_note: Four, the Budge Dragon's own level. In the pool at +0 and out of it for anything smaller. See shared/Loot.Affordable.
stats.walk_speed_note: Ten, which is the column boots have and nothing else does, and which OpenMU only writes onto the item where it is above nought. Nothing here reads it: a character's walk is the rig's clip at the client's speed, and a boot does not change it. Recorded because it is in the row.
stats.defense_note: Three points of defence, one more than the gloves, in the row and not read by anything yet - the fight does not see worn armour. Flagged rather than left to look implemented.
stats.classes_from: The last three ints of the call are 1, 0, 0 - the Dark Wizard alone, as the Pad Gloves. Twenty strength.

sheet_from: Data/Player/boots_04.OZJ (64x64), Data/Player/hide.jpg and Data/Player/boots_04b.ozt (32x32), from MuMain. The .bmd names boots_04.jpg, hide.jpg and boots_04b.tga; 122 of the 132 triangles are on the first, 6 on hide and 4 on the fins.
sheet_note:
boots_04 is the boot from two sides, mean (117, 105, 95): a gold-brass greave with a raised knotwork pattern and a ring of tassels at the top, a plainer brass shin below it, and violet-and-pink cloth in the margins - the same palette as gloves_04, which is the same set. boots_04b is four gilt spikes on black, pointing up and left, lit gold along one edge and dark along the other: fins that stand off the boot on two crossed quads, so the black is the part that is not there.

hide is MU capping the openings, a 9x9 solid black, as on ArmorMale10.
cutout_from: Declared, not detected, as docs/items-and-armour.md says. Here the alpha is real - decode_texture reads it as present and cutting 65% - unlike guard_hair, whose alpha is zero everywhere and had to be keyed off brightness. Four triangles on a 32-square: two quads, and each fin is drawn once and cut round.
material_note: brass on all four islands, over the profile's leather. Islands 0 and 1 are the two boots, each one island running the whole width of boots_04: a gilt greave with knotwork over violet cloth, brass being most of it, as on the Pad Gloves. Islands 2 and 3 are the fins - two triangles each, sampling the whole of boots_04b - and those are gilt spikes with nothing else on them, so brass is exact there and approximate on the boots.
open_question: Same as the Pad Gloves: the cloth margins are on the boot's island and the island is the unit, so they ship as brass-roughness violet. And one of its own: the fins are two quads crossed, cut round by alpha, and brass carries a cast grain at scale 340 - on a 32-square spike that is a few texels of pitting across an edge that MU drew as a clean gold line. If the fins look chewed under --lighting=1, they want a smooth material rather than a cast one, and nothing in the library is a smooth yellow metal yet.
